reference.label: Fibre break
reference.definition: A physical break in an optical fibre span that prevents light from passing.
reference.example: A cable cut between amplifier sites leaves the downstream receiver dark.

reference.label: Fibre loss increase
reference.definition: An increase in attenuation on a fibre span caused by a bend, splice, stress, or similar defect.
reference.example: A severe bend adds 7 dB of span loss and lowers received power.

reference.label: Disconnected optical connector
reference.definition: An unplugged connector or patch cord that opens an optical path.
reference.example: A technician removes the patch cord feeding a preamplifier, leaving its input dark.

reference.label: Dirty optical connector
reference.definition: Connector contamination that introduces optical loss or reflection without opening the path completely.
reference.example: Dust on an LC connector adds loss and raises pre-FEC errors.

reference.label: Amplifier pump failure
reference.definition: Failure of an optical amplifier's pump laser, leaving input light present but preventing amplified output.
reference.example: A preamplifier receives light but produces no output after its pump fails.

reference.label: Amplifier unit failure
reference.definition: A complete amplifier-unit failure, distinct from a specifically identified pump-laser failure, that removes its output.
reference.example: An internal power-supply fault makes an inline amplifier output go dark.

reference.label: Amplifier gain loss
reference.definition: A reduction of amplifier gain below its configured set point.
reference.example: An amplifier set for 20 dB gain delivers only 17 dB.

reference.label: Amplifier noise increase
reference.definition: An increase in noise contributed by an amplifier that reduces downstream OSNR.
reference.example: An ageing amplifier's noise figure rises by 2 dB and increases pre-FEC errors.

reference.label: Amplifier gain tilt
reference.definition: A non-flat amplifier gain profile that gives different wavelengths different gain.
reference.example: Channels at the low-frequency band edge receive 3 dB less gain than central channels.

reference.label: Pump ageing
reference.definition: Progressive pump deterioration that requires increasing drive current to maintain amplifier gain.
reference.example: Pump current rises from 100% to 118% of its beginning-of-life value while gain remains constant.

reference.label: Transmit laser failure
reference.definition: Failure of a line transmitter's laser that removes its transmitted optical channel.
reference.example: A transponder laser shuts down and the remote receiver loses that wavelength.

reference.label: Card failure
reference.definition: A complete equipment-card hardware failure that removes traffic and valid monitoring from the card.
reference.example: A line card loses power, stops carrying traffic, and ceases reporting telemetry.

reference.label: Receiver degradation
reference.definition: Deterioration local to one optical receiver that adds a reception penalty without impairing the shared path.
reference.example: One degraded photodiode reports errors while another receiver on the same path remains normal.

reference.label: Transmit laser ageing
reference.definition: Progressive transmitter-laser deterioration indicated by increasing bias current.
reference.example: Laser bias rises by 0.4% per day while optical output remains in range.

reference.label: Channel margin erosion
reference.definition: A slow decline in an optical channel's operating margin before an outage occurs.
reference.example: A channel's margin falls by 0.1 dB per day over several weeks.

reference.label: WSS attenuation drift
reference.definition: A change in a WSS attenuation setting that alters the power of a selected channel.
reference.example: A WSS setting drifts from 3 dB to 6 dB and weakens one routed channel.

reference.label: WSS passband shift
reference.definition: Frequency offset of a WSS passband that creates filtering penalty on a channel, potentially with normal measured power.
reference.example: A passband shifts away from a 193.1 THz carrier and raises errors despite nominal power.

reference.label: WSS input-port failure
reference.definition: Failure of a WSS directional input port that blocks all channels arriving through that port.
reference.example: Failure of the east-degree input blocks its eight channels while west-degree traffic continues.

reference.label: Differential group delay increase
reference.definition: An increase in path differential group delay that creates polarization-mode-dispersion impairment.
reference.example: Changing fibre conditions raise DGD from 5 ps to 35 ps.

reference.label: State-of-polarisation transient
reference.definition: A rapid change in optical state of polarisation that may exceed receiver tracking capability.
reference.example: An aerial-fibre disturbance rotates polarisation faster than the coherent receiver can track.

reference.label: Mechanical disturbance
reference.definition: A brief physical disturbance of fibre or a patch panel that causes a transient optical-loss excursion.
reference.example: Movement of a patch panel causes a one-second power dip.

reference.label: Channel-loading transient
reference.definition: A brief OMS power excursion caused by adding or removing wavelength channels.
reference.example: Adding ten channels causes a short power swing before amplifier control settles.

reference.label: Protection-switch interruption
reference.definition: A brief service interruption occurring while protection selection changes paths.
reference.example: Traffic is interrupted for 35 ms while the selector moves to the protection path.

reference.label: OTN switch-fabric failure
reference.definition: Failure of an OTN switch's ODU cross-connect fabric that interrupts ODUs traversing it.
reference.example: A fabric ASIC failure interrupts every ODU cross-connected through the switch.

reference.label: Wrong ODU cross-connection
reference.definition: An erroneous ODU cross-connect configuration that delivers an ODU to an unintended destination.
reference.example: An ODU intended for port 2 is configured to egress on port 7.

reference.label: Client-port failure
reference.definition: Failure of a client-facing port or its optic that takes down the associated client service.
reference.example: A failed 100GE pluggable removes the service mapped through its client port.

reference.label: Instrument misreport
reference.definition: A monitoring instrument reports a value that differs from the actual quantity.
reference.example: A power monitor reports -20 dBm while a calibrated meter measures -10 dBm.

reference.label: Stale telemetry
reference.definition: A monitor repeatedly reports an old frozen value instead of current measurements.
reference.example: Received power remains fixed in telemetry after the optical input has changed.

reference.label: Unspecified upstream failure
reference.definition: An unspecified failure somewhere upstream on the signal path, used when no particular mechanism is identified.
reference.example: Loss of signal is attributed to an upstream failure pending localisation.

reference.label: Unspecified server-layer failure
reference.definition: An unspecified failure in a server layer on which an ODU path depends.
reference.example: A client outage is attributed to a server-layer failure before the affected span is known.

reference.label: Generic equipment failure
reference.definition: A hardware failure identified only to an equipment class, with no more specific mechanism known.
reference.example: A card alarm identifies hardware failure without distinguishing a processor fault from a power fault.

reference.label: Optical signal loss
reference.definition: Absence of optical energy, or power below the receiver's detection threshold, at a receiver input.
reference.example: After a fibre cut, the line receiver reads no input power.

reference.label: Low optical power
reference.definition: Optical power below its expected operating level while some signal may remain present.
reference.example: A channel is measured at -18 dBm instead of its expected -10 dBm.

reference.label: OSC loss
reference.definition: Absence of the optical supervisory channel on one fibre section, which is terminated and regenerated at amplifier sites.
reference.example: An inline amplifier receives no OSC from the immediately upstream span.

reference.label: Optical power excursion
reference.definition: A brief optical-power dip or swing lasting seconds or less.
reference.example: Channel loading causes total OMS power to dip for half a second.

reference.label: Low OSNR
reference.definition: An optical state in which signal-to-noise ratio is below its expected level because of loss or added noise.
reference.example: The channel retains nominal output power but its OSNR is 4 dB below baseline.

reference.label: Fast polarisation change
reference.definition: A received state of polarisation changing too rapidly for reliable receiver tracking.
reference.example: Rapid polarisation rotation causes a burst of errored seconds.

reference.label: High differential group delay
reference.definition: Differential group delay elevated enough to impair coherent reception.
reference.example: A receiver reports 35 ps DGD and loses framing.

reference.label: Filtering penalty
reference.definition: Signal-quality degradation from spectral narrowing or passband misalignment, typically without reduced total channel power.
reference.example: A shifted WSS passband lowers Q-factor while channel power remains nominal.

reference.label: Receiver-local penalty
reference.definition: A signal penalty confined to one receiver that does not propagate along the optical path.
reference.example: Only one receiver reports elevated errors on an otherwise healthy channel.

reference.label: Unit down
reference.definition: A failed equipment unit that carries no traffic and supplies no valid monitoring data.
reference.example: A powered-down line card loses its traffic and stops updating counters.

reference.label: OTU frame loss
reference.definition: Loss of OTU frame alignment at a line receiver, whether light is absent or severely impaired.
reference.example: High DGD prevents OTU header recognition and the receiver loses frame alignment.

reference.label: OTU signal degrade
reference.definition: Pre-FEC errors above the degrade threshold while OTU frame alignment remains present.
reference.example: Pre-FEC BER reaches 2×10^-3 and triggers a signal-degrade indication.

reference.label: ODU alarm indication signal
reference.definition: A standardized ODU failure pattern carried downstream in place of unavailable payload.
reference.example: An OTU frame loss causes ODU-AIS to travel toward the client endpoint.

reference.label: Misrouted ODU
reference.definition: An ODU delivered from the wrong source or to the wrong destination by a cross-connect.
reference.example: A port expecting CUSTOMER_A receives CUSTOMER_B's ODU.

reference.label: Client service down
reference.definition: Interruption of a client service in the affected direction.
reference.example: A failed client optic takes the mapped 100GE service down.

reference.label: Brief client-service hit
reference.definition: A short interruption of client traffic, commonly during a protection switch.
reference.example: A protected service drops for 35 ms while paths are switched.

reference.label: Equipment defect
reference.definition: A declared internal unit-level equipment defect.
reference.example: A failed FPGA self-test causes the card to declare dEQ.

reference.label: Traffic-alarm masking
reference.definition: Suppression of secondary traffic alarms because a higher-level equipment alarm identifies the primary failure.
reference.example: OTU alarms from a dead card are masked after its equipment-failure alarm is raised.

reference.label: Errored seconds
reference.definition: Seconds containing one or more received bit or block errors.
reference.example: A polarisation transient produces errors during 12 seconds of a monitoring interval.

reference.label: Backward defect indication
reference.definition: A defect indication sent toward the remote transmitter to report a problem detected by the receiving end.
reference.example: Site B loses OTU framing and sends BDI back to site A.

reference.label: Monitoring silence
reference.definition: Absence of telemetry or status reports from a failed or unreachable unit.
reference.example: After a card loses power, its performance counters stop updating.

reference.label: Normal optical power
reference.definition: Measured optical power within its expected operating range.
reference.example: A filtered channel still measures its nominal -5 dBm.

reference.label: Signal quality reduction
reference.definition: Degradation of usable optical signal quality while a signal is still received.
reference.example: Low OSNR produces pre-FEC errors even though light remains present.

reference.label: ROADM-port blockage
reference.definition: Prevention of all channels on one ROADM directional input from passing.
reference.example: A failed east-degree WSS input blocks all wavelengths arriving from the east.

reference.label: Optical re-levelling
reference.definition: Restoration of an incoming signal to target power by node gain or attenuation control.
reference.example: A channel arriving 5 dB low leaves the node at its configured level.

reference.label: Residual OSNR loss after re-levelling
reference.definition: OSNR degradation that remains after optical power has been restored to nominal level.
reference.example: An amplifier restores power to 0 dBm but cannot recover the 4 dB of lost OSNR.

reference.label: Dark optical output
reference.definition: Absence of optical energy at a unit's output port.
reference.example: A failed booster has normal input power and zero output power.

reference.label: Amplifier gain out of range
reference.definition: Actual amplifier gain differing from its configured set point beyond the allowed tolerance.
reference.example: Measured gain of 17.5 dB against a 20 dB set point is out of range.
synonyms: gain more than 2 dB from set point

reference.label: Pump end-of-life threshold
reference.definition: Pump drive current exceeding the defined percentage of its beginning-of-life value.
reference.example: A pump requiring 122% of its original current crosses the end-of-life threshold.

reference.label: ODU trail-trace mismatch
reference.definition: A mismatch between the received ODU trail identifier and the identifier expected at the destination.
reference.example: The expected trace is CUSTOMER_A but the received trace is CUSTOMER_B.

reference.label: Protection path active
reference.definition: A protection state in which service traffic is selected from the protection ODU path.
reference.example: After working-path failure, the selector carries traffic over the standby route.

reference.label: Protection path unavailable
reference.definition: A state in which the protection ODU path has failed and cannot provide redundancy.
reference.example: Loss of signal on the standby route makes protection unavailable.

reference.label: No optical symptom
reference.definition: Absence of abnormal optical power or quality despite a logical routing or payload fault.
reference.example: A misrouted ODU has normal power and OSNR but the wrong trail trace.

reference.label: Amplifier input power
reference.definition: Aggregate optical power across all wavelengths at an amplifier input.
reference.example: A line amplifier reports total input power of -8 dBm.

reference.label: Amplifier output power
reference.definition: Aggregate optical power across all wavelengths at an amplifier output.
reference.example: A booster reports total output power of +20 dBm.

reference.label: Pump current percentage
reference.definition: Amplifier pump drive current expressed as a percentage of its beginning-of-life value.
reference.example: An ageing preamplifier reports pump current at 118%.

reference.label: Laser bias percentage
reference.definition: Transmitter-laser bias current expressed as a percentage of its beginning-of-life value.
reference.example: A transmitter reports laser bias at 112% of its initial value.

reference.label: OCM channel power
reference.definition: Power of an individual wavelength measured by a ROADM optical channel monitor.
reference.example: The ROADM monitor reports the 193.1 THz channel at -4.8 dBm.

reference.label: OCM OSNR
reference.definition: Per-channel OSNR measured or estimated by an optical channel monitor at a ROADM.
reference.example: A ROADM channel monitor reports 18.7 dB OSNR for 193.1 THz.

reference.label: Received optical power
reference.definition: Optical power measured at a line receiver input.
reference.example: A coherent receiver reports -14.2 dBm input power.

reference.label: Received-power PM15
reference.definition: Received optical-power statistics accumulated in 15-minute performance-monitoring bins.
reference.example: The 10:00–10:15 bin records a minimum received power of -15.1 dBm.

reference.label: Line errored-seconds PM15
reference.definition: Count of line-side errored seconds accumulated in a 15-minute bin.
reference.example: The latest 15-minute bin contains 12 errored seconds.

reference.label: Receiver-estimated OSNR
reference.definition: OSNR estimated by a coherent receiver's digital signal processor rather than by a ROADM channel monitor.
reference.example: The coherent DSP estimates received OSNR as 17.9 dB.

reference.label: Pre-FEC bit error ratio
reference.definition: Bit error ratio measured before forward-error correction at a coherent receiver.
reference.example: The receiver reports a pre-FEC BER of 1.6×10^-3.

reference.label: Differential group delay
reference.definition: Differential group delay estimated for a received optical channel.
reference.example: The coherent DSP reports DGD of 28 ps.

reference.label: Polarisation change rate
reference.definition: Rate of change of the received state of polarisation estimated by a coherent receiver.
reference.example: The measured SOP rate exceeds the receiver's tracking threshold.

reference.label: Client errored-seconds PM15
reference.definition: Client-side errored seconds accumulated in a 15-minute bin.
reference.example: A 100GE port reports four client errored seconds for the interval.

reference.label: Client unavailable-seconds PM15
reference.definition: Client-side unavailable seconds accumulated in a 15-minute bin.
reference.example: A failed client port records 900 unavailable seconds in a full bin.

reference.label: OSC presence
reference.definition: A status indicating whether the optical supervisory channel is present at an input.
reference.example: An amplifier reports OSC presence as false after an upstream break.

reference.label: Alarm-only monitor
reference.definition: A monitor that raises a discrete alarm but does not expose a measured value.
reference.example: An OSC receiver reports loss status without publishing optical power.

reference.label: Optical amplifier
reference.definition: An optical line amplifier that increases WDM signal power.
reference.example: An EDFA amplifies all channels carried on a long-haul span.

reference.label: Booster amplifier
reference.definition: An amplifier at the transmitting end of an optical multiplex section, after the ROADM.
reference.example: A booster raises launch power before the WDM signal enters the fibre.

reference.label: Inline amplifier
reference.definition: An optical amplifier at an intermediate site along a multiplex section.
reference.example: An inline amplifier restores WDM power at the midpoint of a route.

reference.label: Preamplifier
reference.definition: An amplifier at the receiving end of a multiplex section, before the ROADM.
reference.example: A preamplifier boosts the incoming WDM band before destination switching.

reference.label: Coherent line interface
reference.definition: A coherent optical interface that transmits or terminates one line-side optical channel.
reference.example: A coherent line interface terminates a 400G wavelength.

reference.label: Transponder
reference.definition: A line interface that maps client traffic onto a line-side optical wavelength.
reference.example: A transponder converts a 400GE client signal into a coherent line channel.

reference.label: Muxponder
reference.definition: A line interface that multiplexes multiple lower-rate clients into a higher-rate line channel.
reference.example: A muxponder combines four 100GE clients into one 400G wavelength.

reference.label: OTN line card
reference.definition: A card providing OTN line transmission and reception for one or more carried ODUs.
reference.example: An OTN line card terminates a 400G OTU carrying several ODUs.

reference.label: ROADM
reference.definition: A wavelength-selective optical node that independently routes channels among degrees.
reference.example: A ROADM routes 193.1 THz west while sending 193.2 THz north.

reference.label: OTN switch
reference.definition: A switching system that cross-connects ODU trails independently of their optical wavelengths.
reference.example: An OTN switch connects an incoming ODU2 to client port 8.

reference.label: Client port
reference.definition: A client-facing interface that maps a client signal into or out of an ODU.
reference.example: A 100GE client port maps a customer signal into an ODU.

reference.label: 10GE client port
reference.definition: A client-facing Ethernet port operating at 10 Gigabit Ethernet.
reference.example: A 10GE client port accepts a customer's 10GE signal for OTN transport.

reference.label: 100GE client port
reference.definition: A client-facing Ethernet port operating at 100 Gigabit Ethernet.
reference.example: A 100GE client port terminates a customer circuit on a muxponder.

reference.label: 400GE client port
reference.definition: A client-facing Ethernet port operating at 400 Gigabit Ethernet.
reference.example: A 400GE client port supplies a client signal to an OTN line interface.

reference.label: One optical channel
reference.definition: A single wavelength channel rather than the multiplexed signal as a whole.
reference.example: A WSS passband shift impairs only the selected 193.1 THz channel.

reference.label: All optical channels
reference.definition: Every wavelength channel in the relevant OMS, OTS, line, or unit.
reference.example: Loss of amplifier gain lowers OSNR on all 80 carried channels.

reference.label: Some optical channels
reference.definition: A proper subset of wavelength channels rather than the entire multiplex.
reference.example: Gain tilt weakens five band-edge channels while the others remain normal.

reference.label: ROADM degree input
reference.definition: Every channel arriving through one directional WSS input port of a ROADM.
reference.example: Failure of the east-degree port blocks all channels arriving from the east.

reference.label: One receiver
reference.definition: The particular receiver under diagnosis, excluding the shared path and other receivers.
reference.example: Errors occur at this receiver while a parallel receiver remains normal.

reference.label: One equipment unit
reference.definition: A single equipment unit considered separately from the traffic it carries.
reference.example: The pump-current trend describes the health of one amplifier unit.

reference.label: All ODUs through a switch
reference.definition: Every ODU whose route traverses the referenced OTN switch fabric.
reference.example: A fabric outage interrupts every ODU cross-connected through the switch.

reference.label: One ODU
reference.definition: A single ODU trail or container rather than all ODUs in the system.
reference.example: A wrong cross-connect misroutes one ODU while other ODUs remain correct.

reference.label: One client service
reference.definition: The particular customer-facing service associated with a client port and ODU path.
reference.example: The affected 100GE customer circuit is switched to protection.

reference.label: Local unit
reference.definition: The equipment instance that raises the alarm or observes the condition.
reference.example: Diagnostics show that the pump failure is in this preamplifier.

reference.label: Local port
reference.definition: The particular port that raises or experiences the condition.
reference.example: A serializer self-test identifies a fault on this client port.

reference.label: Immediately upstream span
reference.definition: The fibre span directly feeding optical input to the referenced unit.
reference.example: A break in the immediately upstream span leaves the amplifier input dark.

reference.label: Immediately upstream amplifier
reference.definition: The optical amplifier immediately before the span or unit being diagnosed.
reference.example: The preceding amplifier fails and emits no light toward the next site.

reference.label: OMS input connection
reference.definition: The patch or connection at the input boundary of an optical multiplex section.
reference.example: An unplugged patch cord at the OMS input prevents light entering the section.

reference.label: Upstream ROADM channel point
reference.definition: The relevant channel or WSS input at the immediately upstream ROADM.
reference.example: Channel power is normal at the upstream ROADM output but low at the next receiver.

reference.label: Upstream optical path
reference.definition: Any fibre, amplifier, connection, or ROADM element before the observing unit on the signal path.
reference.example: A dirty connector somewhere upstream on the optical path reduces OSNR.

reference.label: Far-end transmitter
reference.definition: The remote line interface transmitting the optical channel received by the local unit.
reference.example: Failure of the far-end transmitter removes the local receiver's channel.

reference.label: Far-end receiver
reference.definition: The remote line interface receiving the optical channel transmitted by the local unit.
reference.example: The far-end receiver reports a defect on the locally transmitted OTU.

reference.label: Path to the far end
reference.definition: The end-to-end signal path between the local and remote line interfaces, including its optical elements.
reference.example: A fibre defect on the path to the far end causes the remote receiver to lose signal.

reference.label: Either service endpoint
reference.definition: Either client port terminating the two ends of a client service.
reference.example: Failure of the client optic at either endpoint can take down the service.

reference.label: OTN switch on ODU path
reference.definition: An OTN switch or cross-connect situated along the ODU path of a service.
reference.example: A wrong cross-connect in an intermediate OTN switch misroutes the ODU.

reference.label: Working ODU path
reference.definition: The primary ODU route normally selected to carry a protected service.
reference.example: A fibre failure on the working ODU path causes a switch to protection.

reference.label: Protection ODU path
reference.definition: The standby ODU route reserved for recovery from a working-path failure.
reference.example: Loss of the standby route makes the protection ODU path unavailable.

reference.label: Active ODU path
reference.definition: The working or protection ODU route currently carrying the service.
reference.example: After switching, the protection route is the active ODU path.

reference.label: Baseline monitoring
reference.definition: Alarms and standard 15-minute performance counters supported by every applicable unit.
reference.example: Every line unit reports alarms and errored-second PM15 counters.

reference.label: Power monitoring
reference.definition: Optional monitoring that exposes optical input, output, or received-power values.
reference.example: An amplifier with the power option reports total input and output power.

reference.label: Optical channel monitoring
reference.definition: Monitoring at ROADM degrees that exposes per-channel power and OSNR.
reference.example: An OCM-equipped ROADM reports power and OSNR for every wavelength.

reference.label: Advanced coherent monitoring
reference.definition: Telemetry exposing coherent-DSP metrics and equipment-health currents.
reference.example: A coherent receiver reports pre-FEC BER, DGD, SOP rate, and estimated OSNR.

reference.label: Hard failure
reference.definition: An abrupt complete failure that removes signal, traffic, or equipment operation.
reference.example: A fibre cut instantly removes received light and traffic.

reference.label: Soft degradation
reference.definition: Reduced signal or service quality while traffic remains carried.
reference.example: A dirty connector raises errors but does not immediately interrupt service.

reference.label: Incipient degradation
reference.definition: A slow trend indicating developing failure before traffic is affected.
reference.example: Pump current rises for months while configured gain is still maintained.

reference.label: Transient event
reference.definition: A brief event lasting seconds or less rather than a persistent state.
reference.example: A mechanical disturbance causes a half-second power dip.

reference.label: Critical severity
reference.definition: The highest alarm priority for immediate major service or equipment loss.
reference.example: Optical-channel loss after a fibre cut is reported as critical.

reference.label: Major severity
reference.definition: A serious alarm priority below critical requiring prompt attention.
reference.example: Loss of the supervisory channel is reported as major.

reference.label: Minor severity
reference.definition: A lower-priority severity for degradation, warning, or redundancy loss.
reference.example: A pump end-of-life warning is reported as minor.

reference.label: Not alarmed
reference.definition: A reported condition or status that carries no active alarm severity.
reference.example: Receipt of ODU-AIS is recorded as a condition but not alarmed.

reference.label: Pass-through behaviour
reference.definition: Forwarding an arriving condition without altering the relevant property.
reference.example: An OTN switch carries received ODU-AIS onward through its cross-connect.

reference.label: Per-channel ROADM routing
reference.definition: Independent switching of each wavelength, causing a line-wide impairment to continue on each routed channel.
reference.example: A ROADM sends two channels from one incoming degree to different outgoing degrees.

reference.label: Default condition handling
reference.definition: Handling applied to an arriving condition when no more specific rule covers it.
reference.example: An unclassified incoming impairment follows the unit's default propagation rule.

reference.label: OTU frame-loss consequent actions
reference.definition: On OTU frame loss, insert ODU-AIS downstream on carried ODUs and send BDI toward the transmitter.
reference.example: Loss of framing replaces three carried ODUs with AIS and sends BDI upstream.

reference.label: OCH_LOS
reference.definition: A critical alarm indicating loss of optical signal for a received channel.
reference.example: A fibre cut makes a transponder receiver dark and raises OCH_LOS.

reference.label: OTU_LOF
reference.definition: A critical alarm indicating that OTU frame alignment cannot be maintained.
reference.example: Severe DGD prevents frame synchronisation and raises OTU_LOF.

reference.label: OTU_SD
reference.definition: An alarm indicating pre-FEC errors above threshold while OTU framing remains aligned.
reference.example: A dirty connector raises pre-FEC BER above threshold and triggers OTU_SD.

reference.label: OTU_BDI
reference.definition: An OTU status indicating that the far end reports a defect on the locally transmitted OTU.
reference.example: The remote receiver loses framing and returns BDI, producing OTU_BDI locally.

reference.label: EQPT_TX_FAIL
reference.definition: A critical equipment alarm indicating detected failure of the local transmit laser.
reference.example: Laser diagnostics detect zero output and raise EQPT_TX_FAIL.

reference.label: EQPT_CARD_FAIL
reference.definition: A critical equipment alarm indicating a generic hardware failure of a card.
reference.example: A failed card power rail raises EQPT_CARD_FAIL.

reference.label: AMP_INPUT_LOS
reference.definition: A critical amplifier alarm indicating absence of optical light at the amplifier input.
reference.example: A cable cut ahead of an inline amplifier raises AMP_INPUT_LOS.

reference.label: OMS_LOS_P
reference.definition: A critical preamplifier alarm indicating loss of the incoming optical multiplex-section signal.
reference.example: A disconnected receive patch cord raises OMS_LOS_P.

reference.label: OSC_LOS
reference.definition: An alarm indicating absence of the optical supervisory channel on the feeding section.
reference.example: A preamplifier cannot detect the supervisory channel and raises OSC_LOS.

reference.label: AMP_FAIL
reference.definition: A critical alarm raised when an amplifier has input light but produces no output.
reference.example: A booster with illuminated input and dark output raises AMP_FAIL.

reference.label: AMP_GAIN_OOR
reference.definition: An alarm indicating amplifier gain outside the allowed tolerance from its set point.
reference.example: A 20 dB amplifier producing 17 dB gain raises AMP_GAIN_OOR.

reference.label: AMP_PUMP_EOL
reference.definition: An amplifier warning raised when ageing drives pump current beyond its end-of-life threshold.
reference.example: Pump current reaches 122% of beginning-of-life value and raises AMP_PUMP_EOL.

reference.label: CLIENT_SF
reference.definition: A critical client-port alarm indicating that the associated client service is down.
reference.example: A switch-fabric failure removes a 100GE service and raises CLIENT_SF.

reference.label: ODU_AIS indication
reference.definition: A client-port status reporting receipt of ODU-AIS, distinct from the AIS signal itself.
reference.example: A client port receiving upstream AIS reports the ODU_AIS indication.

reference.label: ODU_BDI indication
reference.definition: A client-port status indicating that the far end reports receiving ODU-AIS.
reference.example: The remote endpoint returns BDI after receiving AIS, producing ODU_BDI locally.

reference.label: ODU_TIM alarm
reference.definition: An alarm indicating that the received ODU trail trace differs from the expected identity.
reference.example: A port expecting CUSTOMER_A receives CUSTOMER_B and raises ODU_TIM.

reference.label: PROT_ACTIVE
reference.definition: A status alarm indicating that service traffic is currently selected from the protection path.
reference.example: After working-path loss, the selector switches to standby and raises PROT_ACTIVE.

reference.label: PROT_UNAVAIL
reference.definition: An alarm indicating that the protection path has failed and cannot provide recovery.
reference.example: A cut on the standby route raises PROT_UNAVAIL.

reference.label: EQPT_PORT_FAIL
reference.definition: A critical equipment alarm indicating a hardware fault in a client port.
reference.example: A failed serializer on a 100GE port raises EQPT_PORT_FAIL.

reference.label: OTN_FABRIC_FAIL
reference.definition: A critical alarm indicating a hardware fault in an OTN switch's cross-connect fabric.
reference.example: A fabric ASIC self-test failure raises OTN_FABRIC_FAIL.
